newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-JACKSON SURVIVES SCARE BEFORE WINNING HEAT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JACKSON SURVIVES SCARE BEFORE WINNING HEAT.

text.p: Colin Jackson, slowly recapturing his best form, survived a scare before advancing to the semifinals of the 60 metres hurdles at the world indoor championships on Saturday.
Briton Jackson made a false start and feared a second would have him disqualified, as happened to Linford Christie in the 100 metres final of last year's Olympics in Atlanta.
"I had images of Linford," said the 30-year-old from Cardiff, who won his heat comfortably in 7.51 seconds. "Starters in France are quicker than they are in most places and you have to adapt."

Jackson, a former outdoor world champion, is hoping to win his first indoor world title. The 110 metres world record holder has sweet memories of the high-tech Bercy arena hosting the championships as it was here that he won the 60 metres and the 60 metres hurdles in the 1994 European indoor championships.
Since then he has been through hard times, undergoing a double knee cartilage operation in 1995 and suffering from continuing knee trouble since.
"It's a long time getting back, a long road but I'm on my way back, slowly but surely," said a confident Jackson.
Jackson's task in Paris will be eased by the absence of main rival Allen Johnson. The American missed the trip to the French capital by failing to qualify for the final of the U.S. championships.
But the two will soon meet again.
Johnson said before the start of the season that he would go for Jackson's record this year and that his opponents had to realise they would have to fight for second places.
"Our duel will resume shortly," Jackson promised. "There will be a hurdles battle this summer."
